newsitem.title: USA: Clinton refuses to rule out Whitewater pardons.
newsitem.headline: Clinton refuses to rule out Whitewater pardons.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Sunday refused to rule out granting pardons to figures involved in the Whitewater investigation but vowed no one would receive special treatment.

"There's been no consideration of it, no discussion of it. I'll tell you this, I will not give anyone special treatment and I will strictly adhere to the law," Clinton said in response to an issue raised by Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole during their 90-minute debate.

One figure in the many-pronged investigation into the Clintons' real estate and financial affairs known as Whitewater, Susan McDougal, is currently in jail for refusing to answer questions from a independent prosecutor about the president's role.
Speculation has centered on whether Clinton would pardon her and others if re-elected, and Clinton's recent comments have served only to fan the speculation.

At the debate, Clinton said he would take the issue of pardons seriously, as other presidents have done. Dole charged Clinton should have no comment at all particularly when it involves the possibility of a pardon for "someone with whom you've had business dealings."
"You may be sending a signal," Dole said. Asked his rebuttal, Clinton said with a laugh: "No comment."
